## Appendix C — Custom AI Silicon Programmes

Marvell's three disclosed hyperscaler custom-silicon relationships at the snapshot date were as follows.

**Amazon Trainium.** Marvell co-developed the Trainium training accelerator for Amazon Web Services. The engagement anchors the Marvell custom-compute franchise and represents one of the earliest and most strategically consequential hyperscaler ASIC partnerships in the company's history.

**Microsoft Maia.** Marvell co-developed the Maia training and inference accelerator for Microsoft Azure. The Maia programme sits alongside the Trainium engagement as the principal forward revenue driver within the Data Center segment.

**Google TPU-adjacent programmes.** Marvell has disclosed participation in custom silicon development with Google, with specific programme details not fully enumerated in public filings at the snapshot date.

Additional emerging hyperscaler programmes are referenced in investor-day materials but not individually named in Marvell public disclosures as of the frozen window.

leadership.key_finding: Marvell's executive bench reflects the deliberate eight-year transformation from a Sutardja-era networking-and-storage chip vendor into a hyperscaler custom-silicon partner under Matt Murphy. Murphy joined as CEO in July 2016 from Maxim Integrated where he had been a Group President; the M&A programme of his tenure (Cavium 2018, Avera 2019, Inphi 2020, Innovium 2022) brought in the technology and customer relationships that now anchor the Data Center segment. The current executive team layers Murphy's strategic continuity with a President and COO function under Chris Koopmans (a Cavium acquisition import), a CFO function under Willem Meintjes (joined September 2024 from Pure Storage), and deep technology leadership across the inherited acquisition pedigrees. The board is chaired by Marc van Zadelhoff (joined as Chair in 2024 from prior CEO roles at Devo Technology and Mimecast) and includes long-tenured directors plus more recent additions calibrated to the company's evolved AI-data-centre business profile.

ceo.framing: Murphy's continuity as CEO since 2016 is the structural through-line of Marvell's transformation. The WPI EE + MIT Sloan MBA pedigree combined with the long Maxim Integrated career produces the analog-and-mixed-signal chip industry operating depth that the company has needed to execute multi-billion-dollar acquisitions and integrate them into a coherent product franchise. The CEO-and-President dual title was held through the post-acquisition integration phase; the more recent President and COO role under Chris Koopmans (see below) has redistributed some operational responsibility while leaving Murphy as the strategic and external-facing leader.

executive_team.name: Chris Koopmans
executive_team.title: Chief Operating Officer
executive_team.framing: Koopmans joined Marvell through the 2018 Cavium acquisition where he had been a senior executive. The COO role under Murphy has expanded over the post-acquisition integration period to include broad operational responsibility across the product portfolio. The Cavium pedigree connects directly to the ThunderX Arm server processor and LiquidIO networking accelerator product lines that Marvell inherited.

executive_team.name: Willem Meintjes
executive_team.title: Chief Financial Officer (since September 2024)
executive_team.career: Joined from Pure Storage where he had been CFO; earlier finance leadership at multiple US technology companies including senior roles at Cisco
executive_team.framing: Meintjes succeeded Jean Hu as CFO. The Pure Storage CFO tenure provided experience scaling an enterprise IT public company through cycles; the Cisco background brings the broader networking-industry finance perspective. The CFO transition in September 2024 came at the inflection moment when Marvell's Data Center segment was scaling aggressively and the AI custom-silicon backlog was becoming the dominant financial planning consideration.

executive_team.name: Loi Nguyen
executive_team.title: Executive Vice President, Electro-Optics Business
executive_team.framing: Nguyen leads the electro-optics product line that flows substantially from the 2020 Inphi acquisition. Inphi's PAM-DSP coherent optics IP and hyperscaler optical-interconnect customer relationships make this product line one of the highest-margin contributors to the Data Center segment.

executive_team.name: Sandeep Bharathi
executive_team.title: Executive Vice President, Custom Compute and Storage
executive_team.framing: Bharathi leads the custom-ASIC business that anchors the Data Center growth story. The custom-silicon programmes with Amazon (Trainium), Microsoft (Maia), Google (TPU-adjacent), and emerging hyperscaler customers run through Bharathi's organisation. The technical depth across advanced process nodes (3nm and emerging 2nm at TSMC) and packaging (CoWoS variants for AI accelerators) sits within this group.

executive_team.name: Achyut Shah
executive_team.title: Executive Vice President, Connectivity (Switch and PHY)
executive_team.framing: Shah's Connectivity group includes the Teralynx switch silicon from the 2022 Innovium acquisition plus the broader Ethernet PHY and switch product portfolio. The switch silicon competes directly with Broadcom Tomahawk in the hyperscaler data centre.

executive_team.name: Mitch Gaynor
executive_team.title: Chief Administrative Officer and General Counsel
executive_team.framing: Gaynor handles legal, compliance, and broader corporate affairs. The multi-billion-dollar M&A programme under Murphy has placed substantial demands on the legal and corporate functions; the Inphi acquisition in particular had complex integration and antitrust dimensions.

board_of_directors.name: Marc van Zadelhoff
board_of_directors.career: Former CEO of Devo Technology and Mimecast; earlier senior leadership at IBM Security
board_of_directors.framing: Van Zadelhoff brings security-software and enterprise-IT CEO experience to the Marvell board chairmanship. The IBM Security background includes period operating leadership of cybersecurity product lines at a large public company; the Devo and Mimecast CEO tenures span the cybersecurity-services category. The chair role at Marvell as the company executes the AI-custom-silicon transformation calls for the kind of cross-industry technology governance experience that van Zadelhoff's background provides.

board_of_directors.name: Bethany Mayer
board_of_directors.framing: Mayer is the former CEO of Ixia (acquired by Keysight 2017), former President of Sony Entertainment and Sony Corporation of America, and former EVP and Global GC of Sony Corporation. Her current director roles include OpenAI, Box (Chair), HPE, and LAM Research. The combination of Ixia (network test) operating experience and OpenAI governance positioning makes her one of the more cross-functionally connected directors on the board. (Note: Mayer also sits on the Astera Labs board — the same Bethany Mayer profile appears across multiple US-public-company AI infrastructure boards.)

board_of_directors.name: Tudor Brown
board_of_directors.framing: Brown was the co-founder and former President of Arm Holdings; his director role at Marvell connects the company's Arm-server-processor product line (ThunderX inheritance from Cavium) to deep Arm-architecture governance experience. The Arm IP licensing economics matter to Marvell's ASIC programmes.

board_of_directors.name: Brad Buss
board_of_directors.framing: Buss is a long-tenured technology-industry CFO veteran (formerly CFO at SolarCity, Cypress Semiconductor) who provides audit-committee-grade finance governance. His director role includes audit committee responsibilities.

board_of_directors.name: Edward H. Frank
board_of_directors.framing: Frank is a serial entrepreneur and former Apple VP (Macintosh wireless technology); brings deep semiconductor-and-systems engineering perspective.

board_of_directors.name: Donna Morris
board_of_directors.framing: Morris is currently Chief People Officer at Walmart; previously CHRO at Adobe. Brings large-cap HR governance and people-operations experience.

board_of_directors.name: Robert Switz
board_of_directors.framing: Switz is a former CEO of ADC Telecommunications; brings communications-infrastructure CEO experience that maps to Marvell's Carrier Infrastructure segment legacy.

board_of_directors.name: Ford Tamer
board_of_directors.framing: Tamer is a former CEO of Inphi Corporation — the company Marvell acquired in 2020 for $10B. His director role at Marvell post-acquisition provides continuity for the electro-optics product line that Inphi anchors.

leadership.board_composition_observation: Marvell's board pairs Chairman van Zadelhoff (security-and-enterprise-IT CEO experience) and CEO Murphy with directors who bring relevant operational and industry depth: Brown for Arm architecture, Buss for technology-industry CFO governance, Mayer for AI-and-cloud cross-board pattern recognition (her OpenAI board seat being the most consequential single connection), Frank for semiconductor-systems engineering, Switz for communications infrastructure, Morris for HR governance at scale, and Tamer for Inphi-product-line continuity. The composition reflects the company's evolved business profile — AI-data-centre custom silicon + optical interconnect + hyperscaler relationships — rather than the legacy networking-and-storage chip vendor profile. The Tamer post-acquisition continuity and the cross-board AI governance (Mayer at OpenAI, Astera Labs) are the most strategically calibrated single director choices.
